target_label: stem part of reproductive shoot system
evidence: A stem that bears the flowers (often a scape in herbs and monocots); 'flowering' here names the kind of shoot, not the flowering stage. Counts per plant are stem amount within the reproductive shoot system. (37 statements in 11 floras; confidence medium; batch 0000)

Moss leaf descriptions (quadrate, rectangular, papillose laminal cells), 2054 statements. This follows the previous decisions on 'marginal cell' and 'basal cell': a cell in a part, expressed with existing classes. In vascular plants (rarely meant here) the whole would be leaf (PO_0025034). (2054 statements in 7 floras; confidence high; batch 0001)
The cells of the capsule wall epidermis in mosses (quadrate, hexagonal, thick-walled). A cell in an existing part, as for leaf cells. (486 statements in 7 floras; confidence high; batch 0001)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of bract
evidence: A bract is a phyllome, so a lobe of its lamina is already expressible. No new class is needed. (56 statements in 6 floras; confidence high; batch 0002)

target_label: bract apex part of involucral bract
evidence: Phyllary is a narrow synonym of involucral bract (earlier rule C250). Its apex is the region 'apex' of that class, and PO has bract apex. (32 statements in 6 floras; confidence high; batch 0003)

target_label: corolla lobe part of corolla lip
evidence: A lobe of a qualified whole (pattern 12). It follows the earlier rule corolla lower lip → corolla lip (C398), with the lip qualified as lower. (19 statements in 6 floras; confidence high; batch 0003)

target_label: plant cell part of leaf base
evidence: Cells of a qualified whole (pattern 12). PO's leaf base covers both vascular and non-vascular leaves (the moss usage here). (16 statements in 6 floras; confidence high; batch 0003)

These are the cells of the moss leaf midrib (the costa), described by shape and as abaxial or adaxial. They are a cell type in a part that already has a class, so the 'part of a qualified whole' pattern covers them; 'abaxial' and 'adaxial' are surface context words. (121 statements in 5 floras; confidence medium; batch 0005)

target_label: plant organ base part of style
evidence: The base region of the style, for example the persistent tubercle in Cyperaceae. Base is a region the patterns can already express. Where a flora says 'stylopodium' (Apiaceae), use stylopodium (FLOPO_0986022). (97 statements in 5 floras; confidence high; batch 0005)

These are the cells of moss leaf blades (hexagonal, hyaline, thickened walls). Cell plus the leaf it belongs to gives the meaning; 'cell' alone was rejected in the previous review as too general. (79 statements in 5 floras; confidence medium; batch 0005)

target_label: bract margin part of involucral bract
evidence: Phyllary is a narrow synonym of involucral bract (rule C250), and bract margin exists. Restrict it to the involucral bract with pattern 12. (58 statements in 5 floras; confidence high; batch 0005)

target_label: plant cell part of phyllome margin
evidence: The rows of cells along the edge of moss leaves. Cell plus the margin it belongs to gives the meaning. Phyllome margin is the safe parent because these are non-vascular leaves; leaf margin (PO_0020128) is for vascular leaves. (52 statements in 5 floras; confidence medium; batch 0005)

A region of an existing class: the lobes of a lobed bracteole, made the same way as the perianth, calyx and corolla lobes. (12 statements in 5 floras; confidence high; batch 0007) Target changed in the second check: Keep plant cell as the part, but its container should be phyllid lamella (FLOPO_0986126), which now exists, instead of costa (PO_0030072). Polytrichaceae lamellae are separate plates on the upper side

Fern indumentum scales on the stipe. The reviewed sense split for 'scale' sends indumentum scales to trichome, and stipe was mapped to stalk; express as trichome with the stipe as its whole (pattern 12 / part-of). (140 statements in 4 floras; confidence medium; batch 0010)

In Polytrichaceae the photosynthetic lamellae sit on the upper side of the costa. PO has no lamella class. A 'phyllid lamella' class would be more precise if more floras need it. (27 statements in 4 floras; confidence medium; batch 0011)

Cells of the bryophyte leaf midrib. PO has costa (PO_0030072, non-vascular leaf midrib) and plant cell; 'cell' alone was rejected only because it lacked its organ, which is named here. 'ventral/median/dorsal' are layers of the costa (guide cells, stereids) and stay as context, not new classes. (24 statements in 4 floras; confidence high; batch 0012)

Bulb scales are the scale leaves (cataphylls) or swollen leaf bases of a bulb. 'Bulb of 2 scales' is a count of scale leaves with container bulb. Fibrous outer coats are better read as tunic (FLOPO_0986041). (16 statements in 4 floras; confidence medium; batch 0012)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of bract
evidence: Lobes of a divided bract ('segments 3, sessile, obovate'). PO's phyllome lamina lobe applies to bracts, which are phyllomes, and part_of bract qualifies it. (13 statements in 4 floras; confidence medium; batch 0012)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of lemma
evidence: A lobe of the lemma apex: a region of an existing class, expressed with the lobe-of-whole pattern. The lemma is a phyllome. (11 statements in 4 floras; confidence medium; batch 0013)

target_label: plant organ apex part of pinnule
evidence: The apex region of an existing class. Pinnule was grounded to FLOPO_0985028 in the previous review; leaflet apex (FLOPO_0986000) is the broader alternative. (10 statements in 4 floras; confidence high; batch 0013)

target_label: spine leaf part of areole bud
evidence: Cactus spines are modified leaves on the areole. 'Central' is the position of the spine within the areole's cluster. PATO has no 'central' term, so a FLOPO position value next to marginal (FLOPO:0991208) is needed for the quality, not a new anatomy class. (145 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0016)

target_label: corolla lobe part of corolla lip
evidence: One of the lobes of the lower corolla lip. Use pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole): corolla lobe part_of corolla lip. 'Lateral' is a position in the series. (22 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0018)

Moss terminology: cells of the leaf lamina at the leaf base. Express as plant cell part_of non-vascular leaf, base region. Qualities such as hyaline, rectangular and thin-walled go on the cell. (19 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0018)

The unopened corolla. Use pattern 12: corolla part_of flower bud. Shape and hair in bud ('narrowly ovate', 'inflated') are corolla qualities at the bud stage. (18 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0018)

Scales on the blade (mostly ferns). PO lists scale as a synonym of trichome. Express as trichome part_of leaf lamina. Abaxial and adaxial come from the surface context words. (18 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0018)
Moss capsule exothecial cells. Exothecium (sporangium epidermis) exists in PO, and its cells are expressed as plant cell part_of it. (17 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0018)

target_label: plant organ apex part of perigynium
evidence: In Carex/Cyperaceae floras 'utricle' is the perigynium (PO_0009044), not the utricle fruit PO_0030097. The beak is its narrowed distal part, expressed as the apex region of the perigynium; 'beak' alone was rejected as generic, but here the organ is named. (17 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0019)
The axis of a fern pinna; expressed as a rachis that is part of a pinna rather than a new class. (16 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0019)

target_label: corolla lobe part of corolla lip
evidence: The median lobe of the lower lip of a bilabiate corolla; lobe part of a lip. No reviewed context word yet for 'lower' (lip) or 'middle' (lobe in a series); PATO medial orientation is a direction, not a position. (15 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0019)

target_label: plant organ base part of raceme inflorescence
evidence: The basal region of a (grass) raceme, described as flattened or pilose; region pattern (base) on the existing class. (14 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0019)

These are cells of the leaf border (limbidium) of mosses, a region of an existing class, and papillose/hyaline/rectangular are cell qualities. PO has no margin class for the non-vascular leaf, so the margin is a region of the leaf. (11 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0020)

Cells of the central tissue of a moss stem seen in cross-section ('medulla cells loose, hyaline, in 12-20 rows'). Narrower: a cell of the pith. No pith cell class exists, so the bearer is a plant cell that is part of the pith. (11 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0021)

target_label: plant organ base part of peristome
evidence: The basal membrane of the inner peristome is the low, joined base of the peristome; the examples say 'basal membrane'. It is expressed as the base region of the peristome. (10 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0021)

target_label: plant organ apex part of spikelet rachilla
evidence: The sterile prolongation of the grass spikelet rachilla beyond the uppermost floret. Its length and hairs belong to this distal part, not to the whole rachilla. (10 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0021)

target_label: plant cell part of leaf base
evidence: Cells of the sheathing base of a moss leaf (linear at the margin, short-rectangular in the middle). Leaf sheath (PO_0020104) belongs to the leaves of flowering plants, so the moss leaf base is the safer whole. (9 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0021)

target_label: plant cell part of leaf lamina margin
evidence: Bryophyte leaf description: the cells along the leaf margin, as opposed to median cells. This is expressible as a cell qualified by the margin region of the lamina. (8 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0022)

target_label: corolla lobe part of corolla lip
evidence: The lobes of the lower corolla lip of two-lipped corollas, counted ('lower lip lobes 2', '3-lobed'). Expressible as a lobe in the lower position of the lip. (7 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0022)

target_label: plant cell part of perichaetal bract
evidence: Cells of the perichaetial leaves of mosses. PO has perichaetal bract PO_0030030 and plant cell PO_0009002, so this is the part-of-a-qualified-whole pattern: shape (rhomboidal, elongate) and papillosity of the cells of that bract. (6 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0024)

The stalk of a fern sporangium. PO has stalk PO_0025066 and sporangium PO_0025094, so the part-of-a-qualified-whole pattern expresses it: glands and hairs on the stalk of the sporangium. (5 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0024)

In these moss descriptions the capsule cells are the exothecial cells ('exothecial cells short-rectangular'). PO has exothecium PO_0030073 (sporangium epidermis), so this is plant cell as part of that tissue. (5 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0024)

In moss descriptions these are the cells at the base of the phyllid ('basal cells hyaline, quadrate to short-rectangular'). They are expressible as plant cell (PO_0009002) with container non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075, synonym phyllid) at the region base. 'basal' here is the region of the leaf, not a series position of the cell, so pattern 04's basal (FLOPO_0991002) is not the reading. (4 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0026)

Narrower: in moss floras 'blade cells' are the cells of the leaf blade ('longitudinally elongate in the median part'). The cell and the moss leaf both have classes. (3 statements in 3 floras; confidence medium; batch 0027)
A vein of the lemma, expressed as vein part of lemma. 'Excurrent into mucros' is about the nerve extending past the lemma tip. (3 statements in 3 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

target_label: native plant cell part of leaf
evidence: Moss leaf (lamina) cells. PO has no cell-wall class, and a GO cellular component would be the only exact bearer. Wall thickness, pitting, nodosity and sinuosity are standard descriptors of the cells. If moss floras are run in full, consider a FLOPO class 'non-vascular leaf lamina cell' (is_a PO_0025606, part_of PO_0025075) to collect all the 'laminal cell' names. (240 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of pinnule
evidence: Fern pinnule segments are lobes of a pinnatifid pinnule, counted in pairs. This is a part of an existing class; 'basal', 'lower' and so on go through pattern 04. (156 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

The narrowed stalk-like base of the legume standard. 'Claw' was rejected only because it lacked its organ, and here the organ is given. A general 'petal claw' class (is_a PO_0025066, part_of PO_0009032) would serve many families and is worth considering. (111 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

target_label: leaf margin part of leaf sheath
evidence: Bamboo culm sheaths are the sheaths of culm leaves; their margins are ciliate or setose. This is a region of an existing class. (83 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of pinna
evidence: Segments of a pinnatifid or pinnatisect fern pinna, counted in pairs and joined by a narrow wing. 'Basal pinna segments auriculate' uses pattern 04. (79 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

target_label: inflorescence axis internode part of spikelet rachilla
evidence: The segments of the grass spikelet rachilla between florets. These are internodes of an existing axis class. (61 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)
In bamboos, the bristles at the shoulders of the leaf or culm sheath. 'seta/setae' are trichome synonyms in PO. The sheath is the whole. (48 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0031)

Cyperaceae floras call the floret-subtending scales 'spikelet bracts'. PO glume (PO_0009039) is defined as one of a pair subtending two florets, so the generic bract within the spikelet is safer than glume. (42 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0031)
Colleters on the inner face of the stipules (Rubiaceae, Apocynaceae). Both classes exist. (37 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0031)

target_label: plant organ apex part of leaf sheath
evidence: A bamboo culm sheath is the sheath of a culm leaf (leaf sheath of a stem leaf); its apex is the apex region of that sheath (apex pattern: apex part_of the qualified whole). (24 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

target_label: plant organ apex part of perigynium
evidence: The tip of the beak is the distal apex of the Carex perigynium; the beak itself has no class and 'beak' alone was rejected as generic, so the apex of the perigynium is the nearest expressible region. (21 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

target_label: plant organ apex part of style
evidence: In Proteaceae the pollen presenter is the enlarged distal end of the style, onto which pollen is deposited; its shape and size are those of the style apex region. A dedicated class could follow if more floras use it. (21 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

The first leaves of a seedling ('de 4 feuilles', '4 paires de pennes', unifoliolate, opposite). Both classes exist; leaf + seedling as the whole keeps it apart from adult leaves. Juvenile vascular leaf PO_0006339 is defined by stage, not by the seedling. (17 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0033)

target_label: corolla lobe part of corolla lip
evidence: A lobe of the upper lip of a two-lipped corolla. Corolla lobe and corolla lip both exist; the position 'upper' is expressed as a state of the whole. (17 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0033)

target_label: spine leaf part of areole bud
evidence: Narrower: a cactus spine is a spine leaf of the areole bud. 'Subcentral' is a position in the series radial/subcentral/central, which the position pattern can carry. (15 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0034)

Narrower: in mosses (Sphagnum etc.) branch leaves are set against stem leaves. If the flora is vascular, use leaf (PO_0025034) on branch instead. (15 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0034)

Papillae on the cells of a moss leaf lamina. 'Papilla' already maps to papilla cell (C269). 'Laminal' gives the whole: the moss leaf, i.e. non-vascular leaf (pattern 12, part of a qualified whole). (11 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0035)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of pinna

Hairs on the culm sheaths of bamboos and grasses. Culm sheaths are already grounded under leaf sheath in valid_combinations. The qualities (deciduous, stiff, white, length) belong to the hairs. (5 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0021)

target_label: portion of secretory tissue part of leaf lamina
evidence: Glands on the leaf blade, counted and measured. 'gland' is grounded to portion of secretory tissue (previous review); here it is located on the lamina. Where they are known to be nectar glands, extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057) is narrower. (5 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0023)

The rudimentary or aborted carpels (pistillode) of the male flower: a part of a qualified whole. 'Aborted' and 'small' are qualities of these carpels. (5 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0023)

target_label: corona lobe part of staminal corona
evidence: French 'couronne staminale' (stamen crown) with teeth: the teeth are lobes of the staminal corona. If the floras mean a toothed staminal tube (Meliaceae), the target would be the distal teeth of staminal tube FLOPO_0986013. Check against the source family. (5 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0024)

target_label: vascular bundle part of leaf scar
evidence: A bundle scar is the severed end of a vascular bundle that shows in the leaf scar. 'Vascular bundle part of leaf scar' expresses it without a new term. 'Bundle scars numerous' is an indefinite count (pattern 13). (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0025)

target_label: plant organ apex part of carpel
evidence: A region of an existing class. 'Apical beak filiform' may be better as fruit beak (FLOPO_0986139) when the carpel is in fruit. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0025)

target_label: plant organ base part of gynostemium
evidence: 'Column' is the orchid gynostemium and its base is a region. Where the base is drawn out into a foot, column foot (FLOPO_0986081) is the more specific class. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0025)

This is the Sphagnum branch cortex ('enlarged, with conspicuous retort cells'): the cortex of the branch stem, as opposed to the main stem. The retort cells inside it are the separate class proposed on 2026-11-14. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0027)

Leucocysts are the hyaline cells of Leucobryum-type costae. The statements count the layers these cells form on each side of the costa. A layer is not a separate structure, so no class is needed. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0027)

target_label: plant cell part of phyllome lamina tooth
evidence: This counts the cells that make up a marginal tooth ('teeth of 1 cell', '3-4 cells each'). It follows the 2026-11-23 decision for 'leaf lobe cell', which used the same container rule. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0027)

target_label: outer tepal part of staminate flower
evidence: 'External tepal' was mapped to outer tepal (FLOPO_0996032) on 2026-11-23. Here it is qualified by the male flower, which is its container. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0027)

target_label: inner tepal part of staminate flower
evidence: 'Internal' tepal ('les internes plus petits') is the inner tepal of a positioned series. It is qualified by the male flower, which is its container. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0027)

This is the stipule of a seedling's leaves, a narrower use of stipule. It follows the earlier decisions on 'seedling leaf' and 'seedling leaflet', which used part_of seedling. Subulate, length and hairy all describe the stipule itself. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

target_label: bract apex part of flower bract
evidence: This is the apex region of a flower bract, handled like 'phyllary apex' (bract apex part of involucral bract) on 2026-11-14. 'Acute' is an apex shape. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

target_label: phyllome lamina tooth part of stipule
evidence: This is a tooth on a stipule. It follows the 'bract lobe' and 'lemma lobe' decisions, which used the generic phyllome lamina part with part_of the named phyllome. The length (0.1-0.2 mm) is the tooth's own length. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

This is the perianth of a male flower. PO_0025600 has 'male flower' as a synonym. Hypocrateriform, campanulate, glabrate and length all describe the perianth. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

target_label: plant organ base part of style
evidence: This is a spelling variant of 'style-base', which was handled the same way on 2026-11-14. In Cyperaceae (Eleocharis, Fimbristylis) it is the enlarged, persistent style base on the nutlet. It is not the Apiaceae stylopodium (FLOPO_0986022). (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of leaflet
evidence: This is the same as 'leaflet segment' (2026-11-14). Narrow, acute, oblong to linear and 1-4 mm all describe the divisions of a dissected leaflet. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

These are hairs on the corolla lobe margin, handled like 'lemma hair' (trichome part_of lemma). Long, clavate, caducous and 0.5-0.8 mm all describe the hairs. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0028)

The blade of a primary bract, i.e. a bract subtending a branch of the inflorescence (Bromeliaceae usage). Both the blade and the bract have classes; 'primary' is a position in a series. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0029)
Both classes exist. '1-awned' is a count of awn on the lower glume (flora_counted_parts maps awned to awn). (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0029)
Both classes exist; the same case as lower glume awn. (4 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0029)
A cell of the exocarp. 'Isodiametric' and '3 times deeper than wide' are qualities of those cells, and the latter is pattern 11. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0029)

target_label: vascular bundle part of shoot axis pith
evidence: Vascular bundles running in the pith (cacti, Amaranthaceae, cycads); present or absent is pattern 15. Use a part-of expression rather than a new class. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0029)

target_label: plant cell part of gametophyte perianth
evidence: The contexts ('cells as in the bracts', 'domelike' cells, 0.2 mm long) are bryophyte descriptions of the cells of the perianth around the archegonia. These are the cells of the gametophyte perianth, not of the angiosperm perianth (PO_0009058). Express this with pattern 'part of a qualified whole': a cell that is part of the gametophyte perianth. The parent should be checked against the moss/liverwort source flora. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

Seta is an exact synonym of trichome in PO. These are the bristles on the receptacle of a head (Asteraceae, e.g. Gaillardia), so express them as 'part of a qualified whole' and count or mark them present/absent with pattern 15. PO's receptacle is the flower receptacle; the head's receptacle has no PO class, so the part_of target is approximate. Seta (PO_0030032), the moss sporophyte stalk, does not apply. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0030)

The stalk bearing a Fagaceae cupule ('rachis and cupule stalks grayish scurfy'). Both classes exist, so this is the 'part of a qualified whole' pattern. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0030)

The stalk of a single stipitate carpel in apocarpous gynoecia ('carpel stalk conic, ca. 1.5 mm'). PO stalk covers stipes generally. Bearer stalk, container carpel. Not gynophore (PO_0006330), which raises the whole gynoecium. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0031)

target_label: trichome part of inflorescence axis internode
evidence: Hairs on the rachis internodes of grass racemes (Andropogoneae), compared with spikelet length. Trichome as part of the inflorescence axis internode. The ratio to the spikelet is pattern 10. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

target_label: plant organ base part of leaf sheath
evidence: The base region of the leaf sheath, persistent as remains, as in palms and grasses. A region of an existing class that the patterns can express. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

target_label: plant organ apex part of terminal leaf lamina lobe
evidence: The apex region of the terminal lobe. 'terminal lobe' is an exact synonym of the positioned part terminal leaf lamina lobe. Where the flora describes an orchid lip, the lobe is a labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) instead. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

target_label: plant organ apex part of trunk
evidence: The apex region of a tree fern trunk: tomentose, and surpassing the youngest fronds. Trunk and the apex region both exist. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0032)

In Carex, 'utricle' is the perigynium, and its stipe is the narrowed stalk at its base. 'stipe' already maps to stalk (C264). Length and short apply to the stalk. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0032)

Scape scales are the sterile bracts on a scape. 'scale' is a synonym of bract, and scape already maps to peduncle (rule C255). 'Scape scales 2-3' is a count of bracts on the peduncle. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0033)

target_label: laminal cell part of leaf apex
evidence: In moss leaves the apiculus is a short point of one or two elongate cells at the leaf apex. PO's apiculus is the palea apiculus of grasses, so it must not be used. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0033)

target_label: portion of secretory tissue part of achene fruit
evidence: 'gland' already maps to portion of secretory tissue (rule C265) and achene is a synonym of achene fruit. The gland count and length are on the glands of the achene. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0033)

target_label: plant ovary locule part of pistillate flower
evidence: 'Loges 6(8)' in the description of female flowers is the number of ovary locules. Express it as a count of locules (pattern 03) in the ovary of a qualified whole, the female flower (pattern 12, female = PATO_0000383). (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0034)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of bracteole
evidence: Narrower: the segments of a divided bracteole are lobes of a phyllome. 'Segment' alone is a rejected generic word, but here the organ is stated. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0034)
A stalk of a stalked sorus. 'stipe' already maps to stalk, so this is a part of a qualified whole. (3 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0035)

A nectary on an involucel. Both classes exist and 'part of a qualified whole' can express it, with presence and absence through pattern 15. If the source actually means cyathium involucre glands, the whole should be involucre (PO_0009100) and not involucel. Check one record. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0038)

Hairs on the Carex perigynium. Both classes exist, so 'part of a qualified whole' can express it. Use the perigynium class PO_0009044, not the 'perigynium' synonym on involucral bract. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0038)

target_label: plant organ apex part of bud
evidence: Apex region of a winter bud. 'winter bud' was already mapped to bud (PO_0000055), and the region slot handles the apex. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0039)

target_label: plant organ apex part of spadix appendix
evidence: Apex region of the sterile appendix of an Araceae spadix, which has a FLOPO class. The Spanish example ('ápice(s) de los apéndices') is the same structure. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0039)

target_label: plant organ base part of spadix appendix
evidence: Base region of the spadix appendix. The example 'often with flattened, staminodal…' fits Araceae, where staminodes sit at the base of the appendix. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0039)

target_label: plant organ margin part of perianth tube
evidence: A perianth cup is the cup-shaped fused part of the perianth (Lauraceae, Proteaceae, Thymelaeaceae), which here is the perianth tube. Its margin is the margin region of that whole, which the part-of-a-qualified-whole pattern can express. If a flora uses 'perianth cup' for a receptacular cup, the whole is instead hypanthium (PO_0009065; 'floral cup' is a PO synonym). (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0042)

The axis of a fern pinnule is its costule, the midrib of the pinnule. It is expressed as the midvein region of the pinnule class, in the same way as pinna rachis (FLOPO_0986065) one order up. This is narrower than leaf midvein. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0042)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of pinnule
evidence: This is the lobe of a pinnule. 'Secondary' gives the order of division and is not a separate structure. It is narrower than phyllome lamina lobe. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0042)

target_label: laminal cell part of leaf margin
evidence: Moss laminal cells at the leaf margin. laminal cell exists. 'Marginal' is not among the position values in bearer_positions.tsv, so the cell is placed by part_of the leaf margin. PO leaf margin is under leaf and so covers phyllids. 'Differentiated' marginal cells may form a limbidium (FLOPO_0986075), but that cannot be assumed. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0044)

target_label: plant organ apex part of rostellum
evidence: The apex region of the orchid rostellum. Both classes exist, so no new class is needed. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence high; batch 0044)

In moss leaf descriptions ('cells of the border large', 'linear cells') the border is the limbidium, which FLOPO already has. Do not map it to root-cap border cells. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0048)

target_label: petal base part of wing petal
evidence: The claw is the narrowed stalk-like base of the wing petal (PO_0025325 exact). The previous review rejected 'claw' alone only because it lacked an organ; here the organ is given. A shared 'petal claw' class (is_a PO_0025146) is worth considering if claws keep appearing, but the base region is enough for length statements now. (2 statements in 2 floras; confidence medium; batch 0048)

target_label: plant organ apex part of bracteole
evidence: A region of an existing class. It follows the earlier rule that maps 'apex' to plant organ apex of the part being described. (173 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0050)

target_label: plant organ margin part of calyx
evidence: A region of the calyx: its rim (wavy, ciliate, cuspidate). 'Bilabiate' and 'truncate' describe the calyx or calyx limb (FLOPO_0986093) rather than the margin, so better grounding of those statements could move them there. (173 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0050)

target_label: plant organ apex part of anther
evidence: A region of an existing class, like bracteole apex. (161 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0050)
A part of a qualified whole, like 'calyx of male flowers'. (130 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0050)

target_label: plant organ base part of bracteole
evidence: A region of an existing class. 'Connate' and 'free' describe the bracteoles as a set (pattern 16), but the region rule still holds for 'auriculate' and 'obtuse'. (124 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0050)

Scales of the indumentum on a (fern) blade. Under the reviewed sense split, indumentum scales are trichomes. Expressed as part of a qualified whole: trichome on the leaf lamina. (77 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0052)

target_label: plant organ apex part of achene fruit
evidence: A region of an existing class: the apex of the achene, expressed with the apex region pattern on achene fruit. (68 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0052)

Part of a qualified whole: the indumentum class exists, and the leaf is its carrier. Statements about faces (abaxial) use the surface context words. (68 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0052)
Part of a qualified whole. The sex inheres in the flower, as the 'male' context-word note says. (68 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0052)

'Female' describes the flower, not the tepal. The tepal is the bearer and its whole is the pistillate flower ('female flower' is a PO synonym). (55 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)

target_label: plant organ base part of anther
evidence: A region of an existing organ, as in 'style base' (R3670). The qualities cordate, sagittate, emarginate and lobed are qualities of the base. (50 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)

The scales of a Fagaceae cupule are reduced bracts, and PO lists 'scale' as a synonym of bract. Both classes exist, so a container rule expresses the term. Some examples list several parts ('bud scales, branchlets, petioles'), so check the clause splitting. (50 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0054)

target_label: leaf lamina abaxial epidermis part of leaflet
evidence: The curator decision maps lower surfaces to abaxial epidermis (R2700). The leaflet is the whole, so this needs a container rule. (50 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)
'Male' describes the flower, and 'male flower' is a PO synonym of staminate flower. Same decision as for female tepal. (50 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)

A floret is a flower (R261) and a male floret is a staminate flower (R2901). Sepal counts go through pattern 03 with the staminate flower as the container. (49 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)
'Staminate' describes the flower, not the sepal. Both classes exist. (49 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)

target_label: plant organ margin part of achene fruit
evidence: A region of an existing class. Winged, cartilaginous, narrow and broad are qualities of the margin. (47 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)

target_label: phyllome lamina lobe part of bract
evidence: In Lejeuneaceae (sizes in µm) the lobule is the smaller ventral lobe of a perichaetial bract that is folded into two lobes. The whole is named, unlike the bare 'lobule' that was rejected, so this follows 'bract lobe' (R3665). (46 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0054)
Both classes exist. The colours (rusty, white, cinereous) are qualities of the indumentum, with the inflorescence as its container. (46 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0054)

Pattern 12, part of a qualified whole: a sepal of a female floret ('floret' is a synonym of flower, PO_0009046). 'pistillate' is already a bearer-quality context word (female, PATO_0000383). (45 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0055)

Pattern 12: 'female' qualifies the flower, not the sepal ('sépales des fleurs ♀'). The sex quality belongs to the flower, as the note on the 'male' context word says. (44 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0055)
A stamen of a male flower. Pattern 12 expresses this, like 'calyx of male flowers'. (37 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0057)
Tepals of male Begonia flowers. A part of a qualified whole. (37 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0057)
A petal of a female flower. A part of a qualified whole. (37 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0057)

Part of a whole (pattern 12), the same rule as 'leaf indumentum' and 'inflorescence indumentum' in the 2026-11-23 review. 'Present/absent' is pattern 15. 'Pubescent' belongs on the indumentum or on the petal. (34 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0058)

target_label: plant organ lamina part of orchid labellum
evidence: The flat blade of the lip, as decided for the lip lamina on 2026-11-14 (pattern 12). Reflexed, concave, elliptic and oblong are blade qualities. (33 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0058)

target_label: higher order inflorescence axis part of staminate inflorescence
evidence: A palm-flora rachilla: the ultimate flower-bearing branch of the inflorescence, mapped to PO_0009081 as for 'rachillae' (2026-11-14). It is not the grass spikelet rachilla PO_0009080. 'Male' goes on the whole, whose PO class exists. 'Up to ca. 60' is a count. (33 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0058)

target_label: higher order inflorescence axis part of pistillate inflorescence
evidence: The pistillate counterpart of 'male inflorescence rachilla': palm rachillae on a pistillate inflorescence. PO lists 'female inflorescence' as a synonym of PO_0025598. (32 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0058)

The midrib of the moss perichaetial leaf. 'Perichaetial leaf' maps to PO_0030030 (2026-11-14), and costa is an existing PO class with phyllid synonyms. Excurrent, discontinuous and absent-at-base are costa qualities. (32 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0058)

target_label: plant organ base part of perigynium
evidence: In Carex, 'utricle' is the perigynium; 'utricle beak' was decided the same way with the apex. Cuneate, attenuate, contracted, stipitate and narrowed are base qualities. (32 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0058)

target_label: plant organ apex part of calyx
evidence: An apex region of an existing organ (pattern 12), as decided for other organ apices. Acute, rounded, obtuse and emarginate are apex shapes. If the flora means the lobe tips, use the apex of calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005). (31 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0058)
The peduncle of a spike. Pattern 12 expresses it as a part of a qualified whole. In PO the peduncle is part of the inflorescence axis. (30 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0059)

target_label: floral disc part of pistillate flower
evidence: The disc of the female flower, as in 'calyx of male flowers' (pattern 12). Both classes exist. (28 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0059)

The stamens of male flowers ('étamines 10-20' in the male-flower paragraph). Sex inheres in the flower, not the stamen (flora_context_words), so this is the part of a qualified whole. (28 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0059)

The hairs of an inflorescence scape (Portuguese 'escapo', 'strap-shaped', 'antrorse'), treated like 'stipule hair'. 'Flowering scape' was mapped to peduncle. Use peduncle rather than stem, which lists scape as a synonym, because these are flowering scapes. (27 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0060)

The filament-like stalk of a staminode ('filete linear', 'recurvado no botão'). PO's filament is part of a stamen, which a staminode is not. Same treatment as 'staminode stalk'. (27 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0060)

target_label: non-vascular leaf part of gametophore stem
evidence: The records are mosses (Mittenothamnium, Micralsopsis, Pinnatella), where stipitate or frondose stems have differentiated leaves on the bare lower stipe ('small', 'clasping', 'squarrose', 'differentiated'). This contrasts with branch leaves. Stem leaves of mosses were treated the same way. 'stipe leaf margin', 'stipe leaf cell' and 'stipe leaf costa' then follow from the region and part patterns. (26 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0060)

target_label: portion of secretory tissue part of anther
evidence: The apical gland of the anther or connective (Acmadenia, Dinizia, Kalanchoe: 'apical', 'conspicuous', 'red-brown'). Treated like 'calyx gland' and 'receptacle gland'. (25 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0060)
Hairs of a named organ: trichome as part of the calyx. (24 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0061)

target_label: plant organ base part of corolla
evidence: A base region of a named organ, which the patterns express. (24 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0061)
A petal of a female flower, as in 'calyx of male flowers'. (23 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0062)
The peduncle of a female inflorescence. (23 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0062)

target_label: corolla lobe part of staminate flower
evidence: A corolla lobe of a male flower. (23 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0062)

Same as 'female petal'. (22 statements in 1 floras; confidence high; batch 0062)

The costa (midrib) of a perichaetial leaf. PO has costa as the midrib of a non-vascular leaf, and the perichaetial leaf is PO's perichaetal bract. Pattern 12 can express the part of the whole. evidence: The laminal cells of the perichaetial leaves of mosses (linear, porose, lax). Express them as cells that are part of the perichaetal bract. (20 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0063)
A bristle-like tip of the stipule. PO awn (with synonyms arista, bristle and seta) is part of the stipule here. (20 statements in 1 floras; confidence medium; batch 0063)
